High-capability API-based VLMs achieve even higher performance with VERA. For example, GPT-6.1 Sol improves pulmonary nodule detection from 10.8% to 69.2% with VERA, demonstrating the complementary benefits of stronger model capabilities and an effective medical visual harness. Our results highlight the potential of visual harnesses as a new paradigm for scaling general VLMs to medical imaging tasks.

papers.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
papers.abstract: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

papers.title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing
papers.abstract: Instruction-driven image editors produce convincing local edits in one pass, but inside an iterative refinement loop every accepted output becomes the next input, so unintended changes outside the requested region accumulate. We present ConserveEdit, an editor-agnostic controller that treats each refinement step as a transaction against a contract compiled once from the source image. The contract separates what may change (the authorized region of each target, with a bounded halo for shadows and reflections) from what must survive (protected content with explicit tolerances). Candidates from a frozen editor are composed through a source-anchored mask and committed only if target progress, drift on protected content, and image quality pass as separate tests; otherwise the step is rolled back and repaired. For any editor, this keeps every pixel outside the authorized region bit-exact and bounds drift independently of the number of iterations, whereas no fixed scalar trade-off reproduces the separate tests. On all 1053 MagicBrush test edits with a frozen Qwen-Image-Edit, masking is necessary but not sufficient. A direct call already alters the rest of the image (12.1 dB PSNR outside the mask); composed through the source-anchored mask, it stays bit-exact there and its DINO similarity to the ground truth rises from 0.67 to 0.85, matching ConserveEdit, so this gain comes from the mask. Next to automatic masks, however, masked direct editing changes a protected face or text on 48% of turns, and masked scalar selection avoids this mostly by abstaining (23% constrained success). Because its drift test names the violated entity, ConserveEdit shrinks the support instead (2% violations, 53% constrained success); in a simulator with known ground truth it raises constrained success from 55.0% to 61.8%. Automatic grounding remains the main bottleneck. Code and logs will be released.

papers.title: TANGO: Real-World Unregistered RGB-Guided Hyperspectral Super-Resolution with Two-Camera Acquisitions
papers.abstract: Unregistered hyperspectral image super-resolution aims to recover a high-resolution HSI from a low-resolution hyperspectral observation and an unregistered high-resolution RGB reference. Although recent methods have begun to address the geometric misalignment between the two modalities, their evaluation is still constrained by the lack of a large-scale public benchmark based on real two-camera RGB-HSI acquisitions with a high-resolution HSI reference. To address this gap, we introduce DUET, the first large-scale public dataset for unregistered RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution, comprising 403 indoor and outdoor scenes captured with two separate RGB and hyperspectral cameras. We further propose TANGO (Two-camera AligNment with Gated Occlusions), which first compensates for the dominant cross-camera displacement through end-to-end global alignment and then refines the remaining inconsistencies with a coarse-to-fine local feature alignment. A learned gating mechanism further attenuates the RGB guidance where the two views cannot be consistently matched. Experimental results show that TANGO achieves state-of-the-art performance on both DUET and REAL across all evaluated scale factors, outperforming the strongest competitor on DUET by up to 2.29 dB in PSNR while requiring 2.5$\times$ fewer FLOPs. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/FagiolottoConSombrero/TANGO-DUET

papers.title: Beyond the Camera: A Tri-Modal Driving World Model for Future RGB, Thermal, and LiDAR Forecasting in Adverse Weather
papers.abstract: Driving world models forecast what a vehicle's sensors will record next. Most forecast camera video and some add LiDAR, but thermal cameras, which still see in darkness and some adverse weather, are rarely a forecast target, and to our knowledge no world model forecasts all three sensors. We study joint forecasting of RGB, thermal, and LiDAR on real adverse-weather sequences of the DSERT-RoLL dataset. We post-train a pretrained video world model for each sensor and represent LiDAR as a depth video aligned with the RGB camera, with densification and encoding chosen by what the model's video tokenizer can reconstruct. A tri-sensor model sees all three sensors as one video. We score LiDAR in meters against measured returns and compare against persistence baselines passed through the same tokenizer as the model. With this matching, an apparent loss of the thermal model to persistence in fog disappears. On all 58 validation sequences in six weather conditions, post-trained RGB and thermal forecasts beat compression-matched persistence. Joint training lowers the LiDAR error at 2s by 2.1m at a small cost in camera fidelity, and only the tri-sensor model's LiDAR forecasts beat persistence in mean error. Blanking one sensor degrades the forecasts of the others more in snow than in fog.

papers.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
papers.abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. This study introduces a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Its performance is evaluated across systematically varied stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations. Statistical analysis reveals that stimulation type dominates regime determination, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synchronization. Periodic inputs induce nonlinear saturation and context-dependent network routing. Although synaptic weights alone show limited discriminative power, they significantly modulate robustness within a given stimulation context, with reciprocal Ia interneuron connections emerging as key stabilizers. The proposed composite metric achieves robust antiphase detection, outperforming traditional phase-only measures while preserving biophysical interpretability. These findings establish a statistically validated, hierarchical modeling approach in which external drive defines the operating regime and targeted synaptic configurations fine-tune dynamic stability, providing actionable guidelines for closed-loop neuromechanical controllers and adaptive neuroprosthetic interfaces.

papers.title: A 5/2 Guarantee for Echelon Stock (s,S) Policies in One-Warehouse Multi-Retailer Systems
papers.abstract: We study a periodic-review warehouse serving multiple heterogeneous retailers with stochastic demand and fixed costs and lead times at both echelons. We construct a deterministic echelon stock (s,S) policy whose long-run expected average cost is at most 5/2 times the optimum over all nonanticipative policies. The guarantee holds when, as in a retail chain with common service penalties, the uniform backlog penalty and heterogeneous retailer holding rates are at least the warehouse holding rate and heterogeneous retailer setup costs are at most 3/2 times the supplier's. The latter setup-cost condition extends beyond supplier setup-cost dominance: a retailer dispatch may incur a setup cost up to 50 percent higher than a supplier order's. Demand vectors are i.i.d. over periods with finite positive means, and demands of different retailers may be correlated. Each retailer selects the full cycle of its single-location plan or a shifted cycle of half its width, under an inflated setup cost, and the warehouse serves requests in arrival order, allowing partial shipments. The upper bound on the policy's cost includes each retailer's mirror cost, which prices the warehouse imbalance created by that retailer's batching. The upper and lower bounds share a pooled supplier problem and add one problem per retailer, giving a factor independent of all lead times and the number of retailers. For arbitrary nonnegative setup costs and associated retailer demands, a consolidation policy holds allocated stock until a dispatch threshold is met and gives a factor below 4.9. On 864 instances built from Walmart store sales, the simulated cost of an integer-rounded implementation of the FIFO policy averages 1.45 times the lower bound and reaches 1.75, and our analytical upper bound on its cost is below 1.94 times the lower bound; both ratios to the lower bound have nearly the same mean at every supplier lead time.

papers.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
papers.abstract: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. To bridge this gap, we propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework that transforms LLM reasoning into transferable decision support through recursive harness improvement. A Jev-style System-1 model enables low-latency action selection, while an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular harness. The harness integrates procedures, state memory, and world models to provide decision contexts spanning the past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules based on both contextual relevance and their utility on previous tasks. Environmental feedback guides targeted revisions and enables recursive self-improvement. Experiments across three datasets show that JevRSI consistently improves decision quality, matching or surpassing LLM agents in several settings. It preserves low-latency execution with favorable performance-cost trade-offs. Moreover, System-2 development interventions decrease as the harness evolves, amortizing System-2 costs through continuous improvement. Our project is available at https://github.com/usail-hkust/JevRSI.

papers.title: Projection of global daily CO2 emissions in 2026
papers.abstract: Global fossil-fuel combustion and industrial-process CO2 emissions remain close to historical highs, yet the recent slowdown in growth is difficult to assess before conventional inventories become available. We project emissions for 2026 and examine daily departures during major climate and energy disruptions. We fit Prophet models to the latest five years of Carbon Monitor activity estimates for 47 region-sector series. We use these models to project daily emissions for October-December and combine them with activity estimates through September. Global emissions are estimated at 38.0 Gt CO2 in 2026, 34.1 Mt CO2 (-0.1%) below 2025. The hindcast-adjusted range for the annual change is -0.9% to +0.7%. Five September-cutoff hindcasts show lower mean daily errors and larger mean absolute annual biases for Prophet than for a seasonal-naive benchmark. Regional increases total 0.331 Gt and decreases total 0.365 Gt, so 95.1% of the 0.696 Gt gross movement cancels in the global sum. China contributes the largest reduction (-0.243 Gt), concentrated in industry and ground transport, whereas India contributes the largest increase (+0.222 Gt), led by power and industry. Heat-period power anomalies differ among countries and can be muted by summer averaging, while aviation and shipping show different disruption and recovery profiles. Resolving the near-zero global change reveals where reductions are concentrated and where continued growth offsets them, providing a timely basis for assessing the breadth of mitigation progress.

papers.title: A locking-free enriched linearized neural network for linear elasticity
papers.abstract: Volumetric locking remains a fundamental challenge for neural-network Galerkin methods in nearly incompressible elasticity. We introduce the \emph{locking-free enriched linearized neural network} (LF-ENN), to the best of our knowledge, the first neural-network Galerkin method with a rigorous locking-free guarantee. Building on the enriched Galerkin framework, the method combines neural approximation with a structure-preserving enrichment that reduces the discrete incompressibility constraint to a graph-Laplacian problem. This construction enables divergence-free corrections and error estimates uniform in the Lamé parameter $λ\in(0,\infty]$. Nitsche boundary enforcement and tailored stabilization overcome the lack of conventional finite element trace inequalities for neural trial spaces. Under suitable approximation and mesh-resolution assumptions, we establish stability and error estimates independent of network width, mesh size, and $λ$, including an $O(h^s)$ estimate for reduced-regularity solutions with $s>1/2$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm locking-free behavior and demonstrate substantial gains in displacement accuracy. In particular, LF-ENN achieves approximately twelve times smaller displacement error than a higher-order locking-free enriched Galerkin method while using fewer than one-third as many unknowns. These results establish a rigorous neural Galerkin framework that combines incompressibility robustness with markedly improved approximation accuracy.

papers.title: Embedding or bridging? AI4Science teams differ more in knowledge recombination than in problem novelty
papers.abstract: AI for Science (AI4Science) is reshaping scientific research, yet how the organization of AI-related and domain-scientific work relates to different dimensions of research performance remains poorly understood. We analyze 489,409 AI4Science articles published between 1990 and 2025, identifying seven affiliation-based organizational configurations comprising three forms of embedding and four forms of cross-unit bridging. Focusing on 2006-2025, we examine two dimensions of research performance: knowledge creation, characterized by scientific problem novelty and knowledge-recombination breadth, and research impact, assessed through journal placement and citation impact. We find that organizational configurations differ only modestly in problem novelty but substantially in knowledge-recombination breadth. Cross-unit bridging is consistently associated with broader knowledge recombination, particularly in AI-oriented bridging, without a corresponding advantage in problem novelty. However, greater recombination breadth does not necessarily align with stronger research impact. Science-oriented and Multi-orientation bridging exhibit the most consistent positive associations with JCI Q1 journal placement and citation impact, although neither shows a statistically significant adjusted advantage in publication in the Elite-4 journals (Nature, Science, Cell, and PNAS). These research-impact differences remain largely intact after accounting for problem novelty and recombination breadth. Our findings reveal that organizational configurations are associated with distinct patterns of knowledge creation and research impact, rather than a single hierarchy of research performance. The results highlight the importance of considering organizational arrangements in relation to specific scientific objectives, rather than assuming that any one configuration is universally superior.

papers.title: Bourin's Crossed-Heinz Inequality in the Operator and Frobenius Norms
papers.abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $0 < t < 1$, we establish Bourin's crossed-Heinz inequality for every dimension $n \ge 1$ in both the operator norm and the Frobenius norm. In the operator norm, we prove the sharp inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ by normalizing $\|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ to $2$ and decomposing the normalized crossed-Heinz sum into $P_t P_{1-t} + Q$, where $P_t$, $P_{1-t}$, and $Q$ are self-adjoint contractions. In the Frobenius norm, we establish the sharp quantitative inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 + 4t(1-t)\|A - B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2$ via an exact nonnegative remainder decomposition, showing in particular that $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ holds with equality if and only if $A = B$.

papers.title: HealthCLBench:Evaluating Context Learning in Health Conversations through Controlled Case Clusters
papers.abstract: Complex health conversations require answers grounded in individual information and currently valid evidence. We evaluate health context learning: acquiring, integrating, and applying relevant context during inference with fixed model parameters to answer health questions and respond appropriately to changes in facts, evidence, or task goals. To our knowledge, Chinese-language medical benchmarks have yet to systematically combine explicit contextual difficulties, controlled case variations, and member-specific medical criteria for open-ended answers. We introduce HealthCLBench, comprising 328 controlled clusters, 1,103 cases, and 4,931 rubric criteria across medical consultation and everyday health management. Members share backgrounds while evidence, patient states, or task goals change; each has its own medical scoring requirements. A 70-person medical team annotates and reviews the simulated cases and their rubrics. Human review of 700 full-context responses from the original evaluation yields 90.5% pooled agreement with the original automated judgments at the rubric-item level. We report full-context and query-only results for seven general-purpose models and Ant Afu. Across the eight systems, scores with full context are 11.83 to 31.76 case points and 10.87 to 38.97 geometric cluster points higher than those with the current question alone. GPT-6 Astra leads both full-context metrics at 75.03 and 60.42, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 and Ant Afu. Cross-condition differences describe score changes under the reported evaluation settings. Response comparisons reveal failures in checking historical information, expressing uncertainty when warranted, and ensuring recommendations respect required conditions. The resource supports model comparison and targeted follow-up evaluation.

papers.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. We extend pretrained latent models with DWD efficiently by finetuning only the last few transformer blocks, training the DWD head with pixel quality losses while anchoring the denoising head to the pretrained model to preserve the sample trajectory. Across latent image and video generators, DWD removes the decoder while maintaining or even improving pixel quality. On Wan video generation, it visibly reduces detail distortion and flickering, lowering warping error by 23%. Remarkably, the same separation also improves pixel diffusion models that do not even use a decoder: a final-step DWD head produces substantially better texture detail in text-to-image generation, and improves ImageNet FID from 1.55 to 1.43, a new state of the art among pixel flow models.

papers.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
papers.abstract: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.

papers.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
papers.abstract: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times. Circuit-level noise models contain many error mechanisms but few firings per shot at low physical error rates, making exhaustive per-shot scanning inefficient. We present CHEQ, an FPGA platform integrating on-chip sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to sample firing locations from detector error models and amortize mechanism traversal across shots within each batch. Under independent random draws and exact geometric sampling, the shot distribution is invariant to batch size, enabling a memory-throughput tradeoff. A throughput model guides joint selection of the Sampling Unit count, batch size, and decoder count under FPGA resource constraints. Across evaluated conditions, the pooled one-sided 95% upper bound on the weighted root-mean-square relative firing-rate difference from Stim is 0.16%. At a batch size of 4,096, a Sampling Unit uses only 4.8%-11.2% of a Helios decoder's LUTs for code distances 7, 9, 11, and 13. On an AMD VCU118 FPGA at code distance 7 and physical error rate 10^-3, two Sampling Units supply 20 Helios decoders at 49.2 million shots/s, completing 10^10 shots in 3.4 minutes without host-side shot generation.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-agent delegation lets LLM systems distribute evidence collection across workers with separate contexts. This creates a consistency challenge: facts retrieved by workers may be missing from the evidence available to the lead for a joint conclusion. We introduce a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler for studying multi-agent memory inconsistency through controlled factual conflicts in Harvey LAB document-review tasks. Pooled across three models with comparable generation spending, requiring delegation increases retrieval of both conflicting claims from 50.2% to 68.7% relative to single-agent execution, yet conflict detection falls from 16.2% to 13.2%. Within this setting, workers report both claims for only 35.2% of retrieved pairs, and pooled matched comparisons show higher detection than single-agent execution when one worker reads both claims but lower detection when the claims are split across workers. Worker-to-lead handoffs are a central target for improving conflict detection in multi-agent LLMs.

papers.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers.abstract: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. Stabilizer-assisted elimination further removes rotations certified to be invisible to all future measurements. A circuit-dependent schedule is computed once and shared across shots, while adaptive caching of conditional Born probabilities and batched execution reduce repeated sampling work while preserving the measurement-record distribution. Across 19 QEC benchmarks, MASQ reduces peak active width by up to 40 active virtual qubits and achieves up to 8,098-fold CPU throughput speedup over Clifft on multi-round circuits.

papers.title: Learning Similarity-Reduced Ion Kinetics across Scales and Regimes in Capacitively Coupled Plasmas
papers.abstract: Systematic kinetic investigations of discharge-mode and heating-mechanism transitions in low-pressure capacitively coupled plasmas (CCPs) are computationally expensive because particle-in-cell/Monte Carlo collision (PIC/MCC) simulations must resolve the inherently slow ion relaxation. In this Letter, we propose a similarity-reduced ion-kinetic representation and a machine learning (ML) reconstruction method for weakly ionized Boltzmann-Poisson discharge systems. Using discharge similarity, the three-dimensional control parameter space, comprising gas pressure p, gap distance d, and driving frequency f, is reduced into a two-dimensional similarity space (pd, fd). A dual-branch ML model predicts the ion density profile at the reference scale and the conditional ion velocity distribution. Taking a 1D3V argon discharge as the paradigm, we use the reconstructed ion kinetic state to initialize the PIC/MCC simulation, which then relaxes to a self-consistent periodic steady state after only a brief evolution. Compared to conventional uniform initializations, this approach achieves a maximum computational speedup of 56.8 times and a median speedup of 27.7 times. Furthermore, the physical regimes of complex nonlinear discharge transitions, including the alpha-gamma mode transition, local-to-nonlocal electron collisional heating mode transition and low-density jumps, are accurately mapped within the similarity space. Similarity transformations extend these boundaries across scales, opening a new avenue for rapid kinetic characterization and optimization of radio-frequency plasma sources.

papers.title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based pretraining has emerged as a powerful strategy for learning transferable representations in graph neural networks for materials property prediction without requiring quantum-mechanical labels such as energies, forces, and stresses for every pretraining structure. However, the method retains a critical dependency: it requires structures residing near local minima of a potential energy surface, which have traditionally been obtained through costly DFT relaxations of known or physically synthesized compounds. This reliance constrains both the scale and the structural diversity of available pretraining data, leaving large regions of crystal structure space unexplored. In this work, we connect diffusion-based pretraining with synthetic structure generation to reduce this bottleneck. We introduce a synthetic data generation pipeline combining three complementary strategies: perturb-and-relax, generative sampling via MatterGen, and protostructure enumeration. Where structural relaxation is required, we use fast machine-learned interatomic potentials instead of performing a new DFT relaxation for each generated structure. We further compare a coordinate-denoising control with continuous-time variance-preserving (VP) and sub-VP diffusion objectives using a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone. The source comparison covers seven MatBench property-prediction tasks, and an eighth task, \texttt{mp\_gap}, is included in the protostructure scaling study. Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically outperforms random initialization on all seven source-comparison tasks. Scaling the protostructure corpus from 20k to 165k under a fixed 400-epoch schedule numerically matches or exceeds MP-20k pretraining on most tasks; because this protocol increases both data diversity and optimization updates, the result reflects joint data-and-compute scaling.

papers.title: Two-Qutrit Quantum Battery Charging through Ising Model and Anisotropic XZ Heisenberg Interactions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a model of a two-qutrit quantum battery composed of two spin-1 systems coupled to an external field via anisotropic Heisenberg interactions. From the Ising model, we derive an exact analytical expression of ergotropy in the parallel-charging case. However, the collective charging process offers an advantage over the parallel one. Moreover, increasing the collective exchange coupling accelerates the evolution of ergotropy and enhances the maximum average power, as measured by global coherence and mutual information. Conversely, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction primarily acts as a detrimental mechanism, essentially reducing all of these quantities. In the XZ model, the obtained results show that the DM interaction is constructive when it cooperates with the longitudinal anisotropy and when the exchange coupling is sufficiently strong. Therefore, by optimising the maximum reachable ergotropy and maximum average power, we conclude that the Ising model without DM interaction is sufficient to maximise the ergotropy. The anisotropic XZ model allows the DM interaction to be exploited constructively to improve the maximum average power through the joint control of the exchange coupling, longitudinal anisotropy, and chiral interaction.

papers.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
papers.abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. The engine is chosen automatically from the instance size, and an independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed. On the official evaluation (38 scored instances, 5-minute limit) the solver obtained a total benefit of 487,237, finished every run within 277 s and used at most 279 MB; 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.

papers.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
papers.abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. And the ability emerges with scale: in one model family, the smaller models make no edit or break themselves, and only the largest improves and repairs itself. Unlike test-time scaling, self-rewriting writes its gain into the weights, at no cost per answer; unlike training, it runs only forward passes, as serving does. The wall between training and inference is a limit of our tools, not a property of intelligence. We believe self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.

papers.title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 92 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.

papers.title: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
papers.abstract: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.

papers.title: Exact solution of the two-dimensional one-component plasma on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma, $N$ logarithmically interacting point charges in a neutralizing background, is solved exactly at coupling $Γ=2$ on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere, the tractrix-generated surface of constant curvature $-1/a^2$, bounded by its rim and by a second parallel at meridian parameter $u=u_{\max}$. A conformal map takes the surface onto a flat cylinder, where the interaction is the flat-cylinder potential and the curvature enters only through the area element; the partition function is a product of incomplete gamma functions, the density is explicit and all correlations are determinantal. The thermodynamic limit is taken at fixed background density, with $u_{\max}$ fixed and $a\propto\sqrt{N}$, as on the sphere; the logarithmic interaction having no intrinsic length, this is equivalent to letting $N$ grow on a fixed surface. The free energy is obtained through the constant term, all coefficients in closed form: a bulk term proportional to $N$, the flat hard-wall surface tension times the total boundary length, and a shape-dependent constant, with no term in $\ln N$. This is the conformal-anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero, tested here with integrated Gaussian and boundary curvatures separately nonzero and cancelling; the model being a cylinder plasma with a specific axial potential, the expansion coincides term by term with the general result of Shen and Forrester, whose universal constants are the quadratures of the two boundary layers. At both walls the density tends to the flat contact value $n_b\ln 2$, from opposite sides, although their circumferences differ by a factor $\cosh u_{\max}$. Asymptotics are checked against the exact solution up to $N=4096$, and Monte Carlo simulations at $Γ=1$, 4 and 6, validated on the exact $Γ=2$ density, show how both boundary layers evolve with the coupling.

papers.title: Auditing Hyperstimulation at Scale in Child-Facing YouTube Videos
papers.abstract: Parents, pediatricians, and journalists have raised concern that child-facing videos are becoming increasingly stimulating (faster-paced, louder, and more visually dense), but this concern rests mostly on ad hoc observation rather than systematic measurement. We present a large-scale audit of hyperstimulation patterns, which we refer to as content-independent production choices, such as rapid cutting, that may place demands on children's developing cognitive and sensory processing capacities. Drawing on parents' Reddit discussions and developmental psychology, we develop computational metrics for 12 hyperstimulation patterns. We apply these metrics to 16,375 videos from 542 child-facing YouTube channels spanning 2015-2026. We found broad increases in stimulation over time, with cut rates rising across all five content categories. Nearly a quarter of the channels increased in at least one stimulation pattern over time. More stimulating videos also tended to receive more views, but the relevant stimulation patterns differed across content types.

papers.title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{γγ, γZ,γh\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8σ$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3σ$; strengthening to $2.7σ$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0σ$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7σ$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5σ$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4σ$; strengthening to $4.0σ$, $4.6σ$, and $6.1σ$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

papers.title: Adaptive Sparsity-Aware Projection-Assisted Spectral Embedding for High-Dimensional Noisy Data with Nonlinear Structures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose SPASE, an adaptive, sparsity-aware, projection-assisted spectral embedding method for feature extraction from high-dimensional noisy data with underlying nonlinear structures and latent sparsity patterns. We first construct a data-driven projection that adapts to the hidden sparsity patterns and the signal-to-noise ratio, reducing noise-induced distortion of pairwise distances. We then apply kernel-based spectral embedding to the projected data to explore the underlying geometric structure. The key methodological contribution is an energy-based projection selection algorithm that is adaptive to the signal-to-noise ratio and sparsity of the signal representation, while mitigating the impact of noise. On the theoretical side, we show that the resulting embeddings converge to the eigenfunctions of an integral operator associated with the latent signal, and the method can remain effective when the signal-to-noise ratio is low. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed method through simulation studies and real-data applications, showing improved accuracy in downstream tasks such as classification and clustering.

papers.title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
papers.abstract: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI. When the embeddings are mean-pooled outputs of an encoder never trained for sentence similarity, this measure mostly tracks text length. In 6.06 million Reddit comments, an uncentered DeBERTa-v3 measure had suggested that only conservative discourse broke toward homogeneity after late 2022. Truncating the same comments from 10 to 150 words raises their mean cosine by eight times the reported break. A placebo that swaps every comment for a random one of equal length reproduces 81% of the asymmetry, and a fixed-content simulation reproduces 78%. The leading principal direction carries 99.9% of raw DeBERTa homogeneity, and once length is handled the asymmetry disappears under every encoder. On 575,000 Stack Exchange answers the measure reports a post-ChatGPT homogenization of technical sites that the placebo fully reproduces, although answers grew longer. A census of 31 studies locates the risk where anisotropic encoders meet time-series or length-unequal designs. A reverse control on a well-known experiment shows that centering with renormalization can reverse a genuine effect. We propose a low-cost diagnostic protocol. Corrected measures show that the two political camps converged between 2019 and 2022 and stopped converging before ChatGPT. Cross-camp replies engage their targets more closely than same-camp replies.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
papers.abstract: Whether a stored memory helps answer a user's question often depends on world knowledge rather than surface similarity. Jetriever replaces similarity search with full-pool utility scoring: given a query, it uses Jev, an LLM-derived System One decision model, to score every stored memory for the probability that it is useful to the answer, ranking the memory pool directly by those probabilities. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, Jetriever places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases (versus 1.6% for BM25 and 0.0% for MiniLM with user-turn indexing) and reaches 76.0% end-to-end Application, compared with at most 16.0% across published retrieval and memory systems. A controlled 20-question comparison disentangles recognizing implicit evidence from ranking it properly: Jev and Qwen3.5-9B both recover 90% of gold exchanges within the top 50 (versus 30% for the BERT-based decision model Laya), yet at rank 1 Jev reaches 85% while Qwen3.5-9B drops to 40%. On a dimension-proportional random sample of 60 MemoryAgentBench questions, Jetriever raises the four-dimension average from 44.3% (ReFind) to 55.4%, at a mean retrieval cost of USD 0.00834 per InMind query and USD 0.03103 per MAB query. Together, these results show that effective utility retrieval hinges on combining broad world knowledge, calibrated ranking probabilities, and affordable full-pool evaluation.

papers.title: Randomization protects the average, not the trial: chance covariate imbalance and a calibration of balance $P$ values at the design stage
papers.abstract: Randomization makes the unadjusted treatment-effect estimate unbiased over the allocations a scheme could produce, although it does not balance any single trial. Chance imbalances on strongly prognostic baseline variables directly threaten the validity and regulatory credibility of trial results, yet what design-stage balance $P$ values imply for bias and error rates is seldom stated. We review evidence on chance covariate imbalance and derive that link under a linear model with one normal prognostic covariate, with simulation checks. Given the realized allocation, the unadjusted estimate is biased by $β$ times the difference in covariate means; in standard-error units the bias is $ρZ_{\mathrm{bal}}$, where $ρ$ is the covariate-outcome correlation and $Z_{\mathrm{bal}}$ the balance z-statistic, so it does not shrink as trials grow. Pre-specified ANCOVA removes this bias, change scores reverse it, and non-collapsibility attenuates odds and hazard ratios even under perfect balance. A worst-balance threshold of $P = 1/e$ marks where the Sellke-Bayarri-Berger bound reaches 1; under complete randomization the worst of $k$ independent balance $P$ values falls below it with probability $1-(1-1/e)^k$, 0.99 for $k=10$. Any balance $P$ value $\geq 0.317$ keeps the two-sided conditional type I error of the unadjusted test at or below 5% for every $ρ$; at $1/e$ the one-sided error in the favoured direction is at most 4.1%, against 13-33% at $P = 0.05$. Design-stage balance scores should be benchmarked against complete randomization, weighted by external prognostic strength, and reported alongside allocation predictability and a pre-specified covariate-adjusted analysis plan.

papers.title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
papers.abstract: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection. Yet, the integration of such solutions in industrial applications is often impeded by data sparsity and trust in model reliability. While synthetic data offers a promising approach to generate the necessary data with perfect annotations, it poses risks related to performance degradation due to the possible occurrence of the sim-to-real gap. This study conducts experiments using the ensemble method to estimate the predictive uncertainty of DL models trained on synthetic data. The results show that predictive uncertainty increases under the sim-to-real domain shift. However, the observed performance drop is dominated by a systematic sim-to-real bias rather than by ensemble disagreement.These findings contribute to the effective utilization of synthetic data in industrial settings while highlighting the importance of risk assessment for the deployment of DL solutions for QC tasks.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: Constant-Factor Matching-Size Estimation in Random-Order Streams
papers.abstract: We give a one-pass algorithm that estimates the maximum matching size of an arbitrary simple graph within a constant factor using $O(\log^2 n)$ bits of space. The edges arrive exactly once in uniformly random order. The algorithm succeeds with probability at least $2/3$, does not require the number of edges in advance, and has worst-case total running time $O((m+1)\log(n+2))$ on a word RAM. Kapralov, Khanna, and Sudan (SODA 2014) obtained a polylogarithmic approximation in polylogarithmic space. Kapralov, Mitrović, Norouzi-Fard, and Tardos (SODA 2020) subsequently gave a constant-factor approximation from independent uniform edge samples and an $O(\log^2 n)$-approximation in random order. We obtain a constant factor in the latter model with the same $O(\log^2 n)$ space bound. The main ingredient is a comparison between the memory states of a recursive sampling algorithm under sampling with and without replacement. We account jointly for the sampled edges retained by the recursion and the positions at which they arrived. Randomized thresholds limit the additional information stored in numerical counters. A bound on the expected work of the entire recursion then removes the loss from its logarithmic depth. The resulting estimator repeatedly improves a coarse estimate while storing only one recursion stack.

papers.title: ASDL: A Fast Vector Approximation Algorithm for Multiplierless Designs of Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Matrix multiplications are one of the main computational bottlenecks in neural networks. The calculation reduces to numerous sums of partial products, which scale with the total number of Signed Power of Two (SPT) values in the multiplier matrix. Minimizing the SPT count can significantly reduce the computational burden. In this context, we present a Sum Of (signed) Powers Of Two (SOPOT) vector approximation algorithm that limits SPT counts, namely the Accelerated Signed Digit Loading (ASDL) algorithm. This approximation algorithm converts ResNet50 10 times faster than its predecessor MPGBP, while being more precise. We apply this method to the pre-trained coefficients of different convolutional neural networks, achieving 80.41\% ImageNet accuracy down from 81.3\%, at an average of only 1.5 active bits per coefficient. This is done without any retraining or calibration, which are typically required for the most aggressive quantization methods. Our approach offers a promising direction for neural network inference with higher energy efficiency and fewer hardware requirements: we anticipate up to 10 times improvement over bfloat16 inference.

papers.title: Beyond Family Labels: A Taxonomic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Prior for Avian 3D Shape Recovery
papers.abstract: Recovering 3D pose and shape of birds from single images is bottlenecked by the long tail of avian diversity: out of ~10,000 species, only a few dozen have 3D-labeled training data, and in-the-wild test sets routinely contain species never seen at training. Generalizing across clades is therefore a central problem. The current state of the art, AniMer+, mitigates it with a family-level contrastive loss that conveys only a binary same-family indicator per pair and discards the continuous structure of the species tree. We propose a taxonomic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck prior on the shape code of the AVES parametric bird mesh model: a multivariate Gaussian whose covariance decays exponentially with Linnaean rank distance, with a learnable selection strength and noise scale. The prior generalizes family contrastive into a continuous, generative form, exposing the graded cross- and within-family similarity that a binary indicator cannot, and brings continuous comparative phylogenetics in as a biology-grounded inductive bias for the long tail. Our method improves over AniMer+ on both metrics of the unseen-species CowBird benchmark and on CtrlAVES3D, while remaining comparable on seen-species CUB. A permutation ablation isolates taxonomic structure from generic Gaussian smoothing, and a rank-granularity ablation identifies cross-order distinctions (the structure beyond a family-vs-not indicator) as the dominant source of the unseen-species gain.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.abstract: We investigate how non-Maxwellian momentum distributions affect the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities driven by relativistic pair beams, motivated by the lack of a universally accepted analytical description of blazar-induced pair beams. Different beam distributions are used to describe relativistic pair beams in analytical studies and particle-in-cell simulations. A systematic comparison is therefore needed to determine how the beam distribution influences the instability growth rates. We formulate the relativistic electrostatic response in the weak-beam limit for an anisotropic $κ$-type distribution and compare the resulting growth rates with those obtained for Gaussian and Maxwell--Jüttner distributions. We require $κ>3/2$ for a finite root-mean-square momentum spread. For the parameters considered, the $κ$-type distributions yield higher maximum growth rates than the Gaussian distribution, even when their mean momenta and momentum spreads are the same. The fastest-growing modes correspond to parallel propagation for the $κ$ and Gaussian distributions, whereas the Maxwell--Jüttner distribution exhibits its maximum for oblique propagation for a mildly relativistic beam. An additional calculation for a highly relativistic pair beam with $κ=2$ finds an oblique maximum of the electrostatic growth rate. The beam momentum distribution influences the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

papers.title: Improving Radio SLAM via Information Sharing: Collaborative Performance Bounds
papers.abstract: This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of radio-based collaborative simultaneous localization and mapping (C-SLAM) in dense vehicular environments towards the 6G integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) era. We consider a collaborative estimation task consisting of multiple user equipments (UEs) with unknown local state variables together with joint estimation of unknown states of the environment landmarks or targets, using cellular radio measurements. Specifically, a posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) is derived for such centralized multi-UE cellular radio SLAM with information sharing, capturing the effects of the number of involved UEs, their geometric configuration, and their mutually different abilities to measure or observe different landmarks. The analysis reveals how information sharing scales with UE density, identifies regimes of diminishing returns, and provides estimator-independent limits for collaborative radio-based environment mapping and localization. The provided numerical results validate the proposed framework in a vehicular system context, while also demonstrating substantial gains against more ordinary single-UE radio SLAM approach.

papers.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

papers.title: CIRT: Calculus of Inductive Refinement Types
papers.abstract: Refinement types are a powerful mechanism for statically verifying properties of programs. They have been successfully integrated into practical languages such as Haskell, Scala, and Rust. However, their metatheory is not yet fully understood. In this paper we present the first semantic model for a refinement type system that supports the full feature combination of subtyping, SMT-style equality, impredicative polymorphism, and (stratified) inductive types. Interactions between these features have led to inconsistencies in the past, and existing formalizations of refinement type systems omit at least one of them. We present a realizability model based on partial equivalence relations (PERs) over a Scott domain, which overcomes these obstacles. We use our model to prove the consistency of a core refinement type system and to give a semantic account of the annotation-independence property of refinement types. Our semantics uses two interpretations: a refined one, which interprets types and their refinements as PERs; and an unrefined one, consisting of complete uniform PERs with a bottom element (CUPERs), which models computational behaviour independently of refinements. We extend the model to positive and stratified inductive types, showing that both are consistent in the presence of impredicativity.

papers.title: Auditing World-Model Explanations in Retail Forecasting: Faithfulness, Accuracy and Price Response
papers.abstract: Forecasting models that read the price and promotion plan explain each forecast as a baseline, what would sell with nothing planned, plus the lift the plan adds, and merchants order stock and plan promotions on that lift. We show that an explanation can pass the checks used to trust it and still be wrong enough to cost money. We define eight checks for any forecaster that states a plan lift, six with a pass rule fixed before any result, and run them on a world model and on LightGBM. In generated store data with known effects, the world model passes the checks of construction, stability, price direction and agreement with sales and with LightGBM, yet when merchants plan into high-demand weeks it states 1.33 to 1.40 times the true lift, and 1.23 to 1.42 times in eight variants of that world; LightGBM overstates it too (1.26, and 1.16 to 1.35). Both still pick the right weeks to promote, but stock ordered to the world model's lift is off by 0.44 to 0.48 of the true lift. The world model's stated response to a lasting regular-price change is 4.7 to 6.5 times the true -0.5, an error in kind that only a measured cause finds. Sanity checks for explanations test whether an explanation depends on the model; a decision needs to know whether it is right about the world, and these results show the first does not give the second. For the final tuned world models of our companion paper on nine data sets, baseline and lift add up under each model's own plan on every window, but a deeper price cut lowers the forecast in 29% to 83% of item-week steps on Dominick's. Across 703 configurations from the settings searches, checks passed were not related to accuracy (Spearman 0.02, 95% interval -0.02 to 0.05). A noisy benchmark of price episodes in Dominick's data is reported as a check of direction only.

papers.title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide semantic features for uplift estimation, but treatment-revealing text can induce prediction shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization (LULR) to address this risk. With the LLM encoder frozen, LULR penalizes dependence between the causal head's trainable shared representation and treatment while retaining separate outcome heads. The penalty uses a variational approximation to the contrastive log-ratio upper bound (CLUB) of mutual information, targeting treatment dependence rather than generic parameter shrinkage. Controlled proxy experiments provide exploratory evidence of improved ranking scores under injected treatment information relative to no regularization and the tested weight-decay setting. Structured-only benchmarks show modest, dataset-dependent effects. On an industrial pricing randomized controlled trial, mean offline lift@0.3 is 0.258 for LULR, compared with 0.106 for the same-backbone baseline. A separate one-week online A/B test of the complete deployed pricing policy records 5.45% higher sales volume and 1.91% higher gross merchandise value than the control arm. These short-term policy-level gains do not isolate the regularizer's effect.

papers.title: Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincaré inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.

papers.title: Signs of Wear: Evaluating Intelligent Speed Assistance Under Synthetic Adverse Conditions
papers.abstract: Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) systems rely on cameras to recognize speed-limit signs, yet existing benchmarks underrepresent the weathered, dirty, and overgrown signs commonly encountered on rural roads. We use generative image editing to introduce different forms of wear into real street-level images of speed-limit signs. The resulting ISA-Wear dataset contains paired original and edited images. Guided by text instructions, a multimodal image-editing model adds snow, rust, vegetation, faded paint, or mud to the speed-limit sign in a street-level frame at three severity levels. Where appropriate, the surrounding scene is adapted as well, and the viewpoint is kept. Every edited frame has an unedited counterpart, and we only evaluate frames whose original is recognized correctly, so any failure can be attributed to the wear. Since the model alters the sign's geometry in 21\% of the edits, all edits are filtered by a geometric check and a manual review. Severity is measured as the LPIPS distance between the original and the edited sign plate. On 716 worn frames, we find that in detect-then-read pipelines, wear breaks detection before it breaks reading. The detector finds only 62\% of the worn signs, even though it finds every one of them in the original frames. Missed detections account for 78--87\% of failed reads, a pattern that a zero-shot detector shares. Given the annotated sign box, as in the crop-based benchmarks, a classifier still reads 78\% of the worn signs, but only 56\% when it has to rely on the detector

papers.title: BlockAlign: Preference Optimization for Trajectory-Distilled Video Generation
papers.abstract: Directly aligning trajectory-distilled video generators slashes rollout costs and optimizes the deployed few-step model without teacher fine-tuning or re-distillation. However, conventional flow-matching preference objectives assume single-head local velocity supervision, mismatching the finite-interval, block-average transition interface of trajectory-distilled generators such as Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD) and Parametric Trajectory Distillation (PTD). Naively supervising individual unfused sub-interval velocity heads across all sub-steps rather than the fused block-average velocity at block starts (DirectAlign) induces a severe training--inference mismatch that degrades preference below the unaligned baseline. We introduce BlockAlign, an interface-consistent preference optimization framework that constructs states at valid block boundaries, queries the fused block-level velocity predictor, and supervises span-normalized transition residuals---seamlessly supporting DPO-, NFT-, and rollout-style objectives while preserving the native few-step sampler. We further build a unified post-training pipeline integrating offline pairs, reward-free semi-online continuations, and online rollouts with hierarchical preference selection and objective-aware block scheduling. Experiments on multi-reference video generation across MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA and an in-house model RefVid-V4 show that BlockAlign consistently outperforms unaligned distilled models and DirectAlign in structural plausibility, reference consistency, and visual quality. Notably, our approach unlocks PDD's 5x few-step rollout speedup for 3x faster end-to-end online training, achieving statistically significant human preference gains over PDD baselines (54.0% vs. 33.3% wins/losses, or 61.8% non-tie win rate on RefVid-V4; 51.3% vs. 34.7%, or 59.7% non-tie win rate on MiniMax-H3) and up to an 82.7% win rate against DirectAlign.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.

papers.title: Faster $χ^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
papers.abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $χ^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
papers.abstract: We present a method for inferring the interior temperature distribution of a solid object from registered multi-view visible-spectrum and thermal images, even when the thermal views cover only part of its surface. We formulate steady-state heat conduction as a Laplace boundary value problem and solve it with a direct boundary integral equation discretized over a point cloud: a Gaussian reconstruction of the visible-spectrum images supplies the boundary geometry, and the thermal images supply the boundary data. We do not build surface or volume meshes at any stage in our method. Instead, we sample collocation points from rendered depth without the pixels at depth discontinuities, and use a density subtraction that keeps the interior evaluation accurate up to the surface. The whole chain is differentiable, and we use it to recover the pose and depth of heating pipes, insulation defects, and the shape of cracks from thermal images. We validate our method through experiments on boundary value problems with Dirichlet-only and mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundaries, using synthetic and real captured data on scenes with challenging topology.
