The Guarded Swarms architecture addresses this by pairing a digital coordination layer, built on Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Nets (TB-CSPN), with an independent analog safety layer that can veto unsafe actuation commands. So far, the architecture has been specified and argued for, but not executed. We present the first executable instantiation of Guarded Swarms as a digital twin built on ROS 2, the PX4 autopilot in software-in-the-loop mode, and Gazebo, with two UAVs and one UGV in a coastal counter-UAS scenario. The TB-CSPN transition chain, from multi-modal sensing through human authorization to vehicle tasking, is mapped one-to-one onto ROS 2 nodes, and the analog layer is modeled as a per-vehicle Virtual Safety Board that gates every command. Eight groups of experiments show that the three negative guarantees of the architecture (no mission from conflicting, temporally incoherent, or unauthorized evidence) hold at three distinct stages of the chain in all 60 counterfactual runs; that threat confirmation is bounded by the narrowest sensing modality; that the safety layer exercises its full modeled envelope independently of the coordination layer; and, under fault injection, that it prevents every collision caused by a forged mission or a compromised worker once its veto is enforced by an independent gate, whereas a veto left to the compromised worker prevents none. The twin also exposes implementation-level hazards that the architectural specification does not address, and it draws an explicit line between the properties that simulation can validate and those that only hardware can.

papers.title: PAISF: A Partially Adaptive In-Order Selection Function for Routing in On-Chip, Inter-Chiplet, and Wafer-Scale Networks
papers.abstract: The growing number of compute elements per chip, along with advances such as chiplet systems and wafer-scale integration, drives the need for scalable and efficient routing algorithms for irregular topologies. A routing algorithm consists of a routing function (RF) that ensures deadlock freedom and a selection function (SF) that avoids congestion and, in some cases, guarantees in-order packet delivery. We propose two novel SFs for irregular topologies, ISF and PAISF, which ensure in-order delivery by hashing a packet's entropy value to determine its path. Packets with the same entropy follow the same path and arrive in order. Compared to a deterministic RF, a deterministic SF, and Multi, three alternative in-order delivery strategies, (PA)ISF improves throughput by 15.2% and reduces energy per packet and latency under load by 12.1% and 11.3%, at the cost of a zero-load latency increase by 3.3% on average across workloads and topologies.

papers.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
papers.abstract: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.

papers.title: Edge behavior of the KPZ fixed point under upper-tail conditioning
papers.abstract: We consider the KPZ fixed point $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(x,t)$ with the narrow-wedge initial profile, conditioned on $\{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(0,1)\ge L\}$ as $L\to\infty$. Our main result describes its fluctuations near the boundary of the region affected by the conditioning. More precisely, in the spatial window $x=t\sqrt L+O(1)$, the centered field converges in finite-dimensional distributions to the KPZ fixed point with a half-Brownian initial profile. The convergence holds jointly at arbitrary positive times, including times before and after the conditioning time. The proof is based on an asymptotic correspondence between conditional narrow-wedge multipoint formulas and those for the half-Brownian KPZ fixed point.

papers.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty. ForceBody pairs the SKEL body model with ground reaction forces and inverse-dynamics joint torques across 10,386 motion trials (9.7M frames, 26.9 hours) from 140 subjects. Each torque label is paired with a per-frame, per-joint uncertainty annotation obtained by Monte Carlo sampling through the inverse dynamics pipeline. We benchmark six architectures (MLP, Conv1D, LSTM, GRU, Mamba2, Transformer) on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion. As one example use of the released uncertainty, finetuning a Transformer with per-sample uncertainty weighting reduces the MAE of joint torque estimation by 5%. Code and data are at https://github.com/DominoAI-Lab/ForceBody-NeurIPS-ED-2026.

papers.title: Finite-key security of BB84 with passive receivers via reduction to active measurements
papers.abstract: In BB84 with passive receiver basis choice (passive BB84) and threshold detectors, the distribution of detection bases can depend on the incoming photon number. Its relation to BB84 with active receiver basis choice (active BB84), in which the basis is chosen using independent randomness, is therefore nontrivial. We establish a reduction theorem that expresses the secret-key-length formula for passive BB84 in terms of an active BB84 formula. The theorem allows a passive key-length formula to be obtained by simple substitutions into an existing active formula, without constructing a passive-specific security proof from scratch. It applies to key-length formulas derived using the Shor--Preskill, Koashi, and Renner approaches, because the reduction uses only properties shared by these approaches. Our result illustrates a modular approach that separates receiver analysis from the security proof and allows the proof of a common reference protocol to be reused for different implementations.

papers.title: Levio: Smart Actuated Back-Exoskeleton via Retrofit of a Commercial Passive Device
papers.abstract: Passive back exoskeletons show promising benefits for reducing occupational musculoskeletal disorders. However, their assistance cannot be modulated towards the task requirements. Active exoskeletons offer opportunities for pose-specific assistance, but, developing these systems from scratch for research can be time consuming. Therefore, here, we present an accelerated design pipeline that retrofits a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) passive back exoskeleton, Laevo Flex, with COTS actuation (CubeMars AK10-9) and sensing (IMUs and load-cell) paradigms. Levio was able to provide assistance based on the user's pose. Nine participants performed stoop lifting with the original Laevo and the retrofit Levio system, in transparent and assisted modes. Compared to Laevo, Levio modulated the assistance provided between the bending and lifting phases of the stoop task. The passive assistance offered by Laevo was $25.2 \pm 4.3$ Nm and $30.6 \pm 9.5$ Nm respectively during the bending and lifting phases of the stoop tasks. Levio reduced the resistive torque during bending to $17.9 \pm 4.6$ Nm and offered increased assistance of $37.7 \pm 6.4$ Nm during lifting. Moreover, participants reported higher usability scores and lowest mean global discomfort score while using the Levio when compared to Laevo. These benefits demonstrates retrofitting passive exoskeletons is a viable direction for rapid prototyping of wearable exoskeletons for lifting.

papers.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content. We propose \textsc{StitchRAG}, a framework for constructing compact context in RAG. \textsc{StitchRAG} builds a faithful, information-dense context while dynamically compressing the retrieved passages. We adapt the size reduction ratio to each passage by formulating a utility maximization trading-off the retained information and computation costs. We then extract answer candidates and query-related keywords from passages as anchors and collect passage sentences containing anchors under the derived size constraint. Finally, we connect or stitch the collected sentences together using text diffusion to form a coherent and natural context. Experiments on five open-domain QA benchmarks show that \textsc{StitchRAG} consistently outperforms diverse multi-step and compression baselines. Extensive ablations show the effectiveness of dynamic size allocation, anchor preservation, and diffusion-based stitching.

papers.title: Universal scaling of brine migration in ice
papers.abstract: Sea ice hosts mobile brine inclusions whose migration influences salt redistribution, microstructure and transport within the ice. Although their motion under temperature gradient is commonly described as a diffusion-limited process, experimental evidence has remained rare and insufficient because migration is slow and controlled inclusion seeding is challenging. Here we introduce an experimental method to trap and monitor hundreds of inclusions in ice under controlled temperature gradients. Using four solutes, three imposed gradients and two order of magnitude in initial concentration, we quantify migration dynamics over a broad range of conditions. We find that, except close to the ice front, inclusion migration is consistent with a regime limited by solute diffusion. After applying a universal scaling, both our data and previous measurements collapse onto a master curve, providing a general framework for describing solute transport in ice.

papers.title: The Koebe radius for univalent cubics
papers.abstract: Let \(p(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3\) be a polynomial univalent in the unit disk \(Δ\). We determine the largest disk centered at the origin that is contained in the image \(p(Δ)\) of every such polynomial. Its squared radius is the unique real root of \[ 27q^3-54q^2+63q-8=0. \] We also find the extremal polynomial \(p_*\).

papers.title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. The proposed constellation builds on a previous structured Grassmannian signaling design, which has the remarkable property of producing space-time matrices with a single nonzero entry per row, while introducing a novel systematic design for the second layer corresponding to the Stiefel representatives. The design of the second layer preserves the sparsity of the first layer and significantly reduces the decoding computational complexity, while ensuring reliable performance under sequential decoding and enabling a simple yet effective bit labeling, as validated by numerical results in terms of bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results also show graceful performance degradation under channel correlation and, for limited coherence intervals where channel state information at the receiver (CSIR) can be estimated only imperfectly, improved performance compared with classical space-time block coding (STBC) schemes based on QAM and PSK.

papers.title: Exploiting Aggregate Feedback for Decentralized Equilibrium Learning in Markov Games: A Smart Grid Application
papers.abstract: In many multi-agent systems, an agent's payoff depends on its own action and an aggregate of other agents' actions, rather than their individual decisions. This paper investigates decentralized equilibrium learning in Markov games (MGs) with such aggregative reward structures. However, existing decentralized learning algorithms for general MGs typically rely on bandit feedback, without exploiting the additional information available from aggregate observations. To exploit this information, we develop an aggregation-predictive stage-based V-learning algorithm with hybrid-feedback Exp3-IX. Using known local reward functions and observed aggregate quantities, each agent evaluates the immediate rewards of all candidate actions and predicts their immediate losses from historical aggregate feedback, while continuation values are learned from selected-action state transitions. The algorithm requires neither opponents' individual information nor knowledge of the transition kernel. We establish a high-probability regret bound that explicitly depends on aggregate prediction errors and retains the standard worst-case order. Under a regularity condition on adaptive stage lengths, the algorithm learns an $ε$-approximate coarse correlated equilibrium (CCE) within $\widetilde O(SA_{\max}T^5/ε^2)$ episodes and extends to correlated equilibrium (CE) learning. We further apply the algorithm to a renewable-rich microgrid with strategic prosumers and shared energy storage. Numerical results show smaller deviation gaps and lower gap-AUC than three learning baselines. Compared with representative demand-response rules, the learned policies exhibit weaker incentives for unilateral deviations while maintaining favorable user rewards, high renewable utilization, and relatively stable electricity prices.

papers.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input. Eleven prompt-injection attempts across five categories were reported as resisted, whereas both configuration-layer attack paths produced observable behavioural changes on physical hardware. We demonstrate local and network-adjacent access, mapping the weakness to CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for a Critical Function) and CWE-1327 (Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address), with a reported CVSS v3.1 score of 6.5 (Medium). A configuration endpoint also accepts cross-origin requests without a CORS preflight (CWE-352; 6.5 Medium), while the persistent-memory sink stores content without enforcing its stated restrictions. A source review of 59 public repositories identifies missing authentication in 10 of 11 source-verifiable genuine applications, or 11 of 11 including a framework-default case. These findings indicate recurrence within the sampled repositories, not prevalence in commercial products. We characterise a deployment gap between developer-oriented network assumptions and consumer-facing embodied AI security: inference-layer refusal cannot prevent unauthorised changes to model instructions. Potential consequences include surveillance through onboard cameras and microphones and social engineering of nearby users. Proof-of-concept code, evidence and the survey are available at https://bit.ly/reachypi.

papers.title: Sharp lower bounds for weighted bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
papers.abstract: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts the sizes of which differ by at most one. We prove that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most an odd positive integer $k$, with arbitrary nonnegative real edge weights, has a bisection of weight at least $(k+1)/(2k)$ times its total edge weight. The corresponding bound $(k+2)/(2(k+1))$ for even $k$ follows immediately. Both coefficients are best possible. Somewhat surprisingly, these are exactly the sharp coefficients known for maximum weighted cuts, despite the additional balance requirement.

papers.title: Robust Actor-Critic Learning under Transport and Divergence Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Learning reliable control policies requires accounting for uncertainty in transition dynamics and errors introduced by function estimation and action generation. We develop an actor--critic method for discounted robust Markov decision processes with continuous states and actions and an unknown nominal transition law. We consider transition uncertainty sets defined by Wasserstein distance, total variation, Kullback--Leibler divergence, or Pearson chi-square divergence. A conditional diffusion model is fitted once to offline transitions. At each subsequent iteration, we estimate the robust action-value function from current-policy observations using a shared-target minimax criterion, then update a generative actor through exponentially weighted score matching. Regularization preserves exploration and provides the density regularity needed for conditional distribution estimation. Under coverage and regularity conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for critic estimation, the learned conditional action law, and the robust return of the implemented policy. The bounds distinguish critic estimation error, uncertainty in the nominal transition model, and policy regularization, and characterize how the four robustness radii affect the resulting guarantees.

papers.title: Effects of probe size, shape, and probe-surface interactions in imaging multilayer island growth, coalescence, and formation of a smooth film
papers.abstract: Recent studies of deposition onto weakly interacting substrates have revealed multilayer island growth, followed by smooth-film formation upon island coalescence. However, for C60 films, the roughness peak measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM) was significantly lower than that obtained by X-ray reflectometry (XRR), suggesting tip-sample convolution effects. We investigate this problem using kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of such films and models of probe-surface interactions for AFM imaging modes. To model the non-contact mode, surface profiles are transformed by averaging heights over regions matching the probe-tip width. A roughness peak remains if the probe width L is smaller than the average island distance, but its height decreases with L and its position is slightly displaced. In the contact-mode model with cylindrical probes and hard-core interactions, the peak also decreases and shifts significantly to smaller thicknesses, indicating apparently faster island coalescence. Thus, SPM images under these conditions may underestimate film-thickness nonuniformity in deposits with coalescing islands. Instead, models of sharp pyramidal or conical probes with hard-core interactions produce deviations in the roughness peaks only for large L, although such sharp tips are difficult to realize experimentally. A geometric model of cuboid island growth and coalescence quantitatively confirms the effects of contact modes and probe shapes observed in the simulations. The results suggest that post-growth processes, such as island coarsening and dewetting, may have occurred in the recently studied C60 film between the XRR and AFM measurements.

papers.title: LoopPrune: Recurrent Pruning for Looped Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped diffusion Transformers reuse shared blocks to deepen computation and match larger models with fewer parameters, reducing storage and deployment burdens. Yet repeated attention and MLP computations remain costly. Pruning reduces storage and computation by removing redundant parameters or units. Training-free methods struggle to resolve recurrent contributions, while training-based methods lack explicit constraints on position-specific errors affecting later inputs and final outputs. We propose LoopPrune, a pruning and recovery framework addressing these requirements. Recurrent importance estimation combines shared-removal effects and position variation to select a shared structure; shared reconstruction pools recurrent input statistics to compensate weights. Loop-position recovery compares complete denoising predictions at identical student states and matches text guidance, updating all student parameters against a fixed dense teacher. Extensive experiments across four open-source models, six benchmarks, and three pruning paradigms demonstrate effectiveness. At 30% structured parameter pruning, Looped-DiT B/16 retains 93.14% of dense six-benchmark average accuracy, exceeding the best baseline by 9.49%. Across PyTorch, vLLM-Omni, and SGLang Diffusion, pruned SDXSv3 reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 34.36-44.64% and accelerates denoising 1.46-1.74x over dense models.

papers.title: Learning Cross-Domain Media Similarity from Amazon Reviews
papers.abstract: Collaborative filtering is a basic foundation of many recommendation algorithms. It works by analyzing a user's history and then suggesting items similar to those in that history. This method typically relies on user data to compute item similarity, data that is widely available to commercial systems but is usually sparse or inaccessible for independent systems and research, especially across multiple media domains. In this work, we propose a method to generalize similarity information between items using supervised learning. As input to our model, we use semantic and temporal features extracted from Amazon product reviews, which are publicly available. As the training target, we use item (product) co-occurrence in the reviewing history of Amazon customers. We evaluate the quality of the predicted similarities across two media domains: books and movies. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness of our methodology, yielding positive outcomes in zero-shot cross-domain transfer tasks. Furthermore, feature attribution analysis reveals a structural shift in how feature groups are utilized across setups: intra-domain models rely heavily on linguistic semantics, whereas cross-domain environments pivot toward behavioral popularity cues. Incorporating even limited target-domain context during training bridges this domain sparsity gap, significantly enhancing framework generalization.

papers.title: Teaching What to Look For: Privileged Perception Questions for Agentic On-Policy Distillation in Video Captioning
papers.abstract: Detailed video captioning requires comprehensive and faithful descriptions of objects, actions, and temporal events. Fixed-frame sampling, however, can miss brief motions, small objects, and other fine-grained evidence, motivating captioning agents that actively seek relevant moments and inspect local regions. Training such behavior is challenging because, unlike video question answering, generic captioning instructions do not specify what visual evidence should be acquired. We propose Perception-Question On-Policy Distillation (PQ-OPD), which uses training-only Perception Questions (PQs) to guide active video perception. PQs specify what should be inspected without revealing the corresponding answers, encouraging the teacher to explore the video more comprehensively and focus on relevant visual evidence. Along trajectories generated by the student, on-policy distillation transfers this guidance to the student's reasoning, tool calls, and captions; no PQs are required at inference. Across three detailed-captioning and two caption-to-QA benchmarks, PQ-OPD consistently improves the corresponding untrained agents across teacher-student scales and input-frame budgets. Under our evaluation protocol, PQ-OPD achieves the strongest primary-metric results among the compared open-source models on DREAM-1K, CaReBench, ShortVidBench, MotionBench, and VidCapBench-AE. Our ablations, together with analysis of temporal coverage and answer leakage, further indicates that the student internalizes the training-time guidance as a more effective video exploration policy.

papers.title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
papers.abstract: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $Δ(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

papers.title: Improved compensation for missing high-order aberrations with multi-frame blind deconvolution and phase diversity techniques
papers.abstract: Context. Image restoration with phase diversity (PD) and multi-frame blind deconvolution (MFBD) techniques lead to remarkable improvement in image quality, but is limited by the number of aberration parameters that can be determined. Compensation for the missing high-order modes is needed to further improve image quality, and to compensate for residual straylight. Aims. We aim to improve on methods for compensating missing high-order aberrations previously proposed by Scharmer et al. (2010) and Lofdahl & Hillberg (2022). Methods. The wavefront is divided into a set of low-order aberrations, which are treated individually, and high-order aberrations that are treated collectively. The high-order part of the transfer function is averaged, assuming Gaussian seeing statistics with Kolmogorov turbulence for the individual aberrations. Assuming that their accumulated effect is roughly uniform over the pupil, we obtain a high-order modulation transfer function that is represented with a single free parameter. Results. The high quality of the of the proposed high-order modulation transfer function is verified by calculating the Strehl from random samples of point-spread functions for D/r0 ranging from 4 to 20, where D is the telescope diameter and r0 the Fried seeing parameter. The proposed approximation offers significant advantages over the earlier proposals. Conclusions. The proposed method of compensating for missing high-order aberrations in PD or MFBD image reconstruction can dramatically improve the fidelity of solar images. Variations of the seeing (r0) within a data-set can be compensated for self consistently during PD or MFBD processing, but the average value of r0 must be provided from an external source. The computational cost of implementing this method is marginal.

papers.title: Reference Coordinates, Output Perturbations, and Information Loss in EEG Decoding
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoders can respond to reference changes that preserve all relative-potential information. We use established measurement-operator theory to distinguish coordinate sensitivity, additional output-channel perturbations, and electrode loss. Exact pseudoinverse alignment supplies a consistency control; measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) denotes a graph-Tikhonov estimator. The broader evaluation covers three public motor-imagery datasets and four decoders. The primary EEGNet comparison on Cho2017 and PhysioNet uses three paired training seeds, three shared noise realizations, and six front ends, with identical CAR training inputs sharing checkpoints. At 10 dB output perturbation, MOC-minus-raw disagreement was -0.144 and -0.107, while balanced-accuracy differences were 0.044 and 0.050, respectively; these four contrasts passed the retained Holm correction. MOC also reduced disagreement relative to pseudoinversion across all three seeds in both cohorts. However, comparison with fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion did not establish an additional MOC benefit. Preserving zero reference rows changed raw disagreement by less than 0.001 in magnitude; inverse-method predictions were unchanged. For canonical front ends, cross-reference disagreement was close to the reference obtained from independent noise within the same operator. Controlled weak-mode reconstruction and equal-rank electrode masks exposed separate stability and information-loss effects. The results locate the complete-reference gains within spatial processing under the specified stress model, while requiring decoding accuracy alongside consistency to assess practical utility.

papers.title: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 Å profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.

papers.title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
papers.abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $μ$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I γ_{Σ_i}(K_i)^{\tilde λ_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}γ_Γ\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,Σ_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $γ_{Σ_i}$ is zero, where $λ_i, \tilde λ_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde λ_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $Γ, Σ_1,\cdots,Σ_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I λ_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

papers.title: Statically Typed Purely Functional Definitional Interpreters for {\it Essentials of Programming Languages}
papers.abstract: Definitional interpreters provide an executable and pedagogically effective way to explain programming language semantics. However, when implemented in a dynamically typed and effectful metalanguage, semantic components such as stores, continuations, handlers, substitutions, and scheduling states may remain implicit in the host-language implementation, making it harder to see how language extensions affect interpreter structure. This paper reconstructs the family of interpreters from \textit{Essentials of Programming Languages} (EOPL) in Haskell, a statically typed and purely functional metalanguage, for pedagogical use. We preserve the object languages, examples, and tests of EOPL while making their semantic components explicit through algebraic data types, evaluator signatures, and explicit semantic domains. Across 15 interpreters and 6 type checkers, language extensions are exposed as systematic type-directed changes. The reconstruction is currently used in undergraduate and graduate programming language courses, where students learn interpreter construction through incremental and test-driven development. We further illustrate its pedagogical use through three case studies that progressively extend students' experience: composing mutable state and exception handling, deriving an actor-based interpreter from the typed structure of the EOPL thread interpreter, and translating the CHECKED interpreter and type checker into Rocq to mechanize type safety. Together, the classroom experience and case studies suggest that the reconstruction provides a concrete bridge from learning programming language concepts through executable interpreters to language design and mechanized reasoning.

papers.title: Shape design for degenerate elliptic Equation with degenerate boundary and its application to quantitativeweak unique continuation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the unique continuation property (UCP) for a class of degenerate elliptic equations of the form $-\text{div}(A\nabla u) = λu$ in a bounded domain $Ω\s \mathbb{R}^N$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions. While unique continuation is well-established for uniformly elliptic operators via Carleman estimates or frequency-function methods, spatial degeneracy introduces substantial analytical obstacles in higher dimensions, particularly due to the lack of sufficient regularity for weak solutions and the breakdown of classical boundary integration-by-parts identities. To overcome these challenges, we develop an alternative framework based on the shape design (shape optimization) method under suitable structural assumptions. We highlight the fundamental distinction between qualitative and quantitative unique continuation in the degenerate setting. While qualitative UCP can sometimes be adapted from classical arguments, quantitative UCP requires explicit estimates that control the behavior of the solution throughout the domain by its behavior on a sub-domain. By integrating the shape design approach with a compatible weighted Hardy inequality, we establish new quantitative estimates and unique continuation results for higher-dimensional degenerate elliptic operators, bypassing the stringent regularity requirements of traditional methods.

papers.title: LaFlash: Capacity-Driven Acceleration for Coding Agent Workflows via QLC-HBF
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve toward agentic AI, coding agents are emerging as memory-intensive workloads that repeatedly reuse persistent states, including contexts and KV caches. Emerging agentic workflows, including Loop/Graph Engineering, cause state amplification through frequent active/dormant transitions, increasing memory pressure. Evicted states incur costly recomputation upon reactivation, particularly under long-context, short-decode workloads. This motivates Capacity-Driven Acceleration (CDA), which explicitly accounts for state amplification to allocate memory capacity between active concurrency and dormant-state retention, replacing recomputation with memory access. In this work, we propose LaFlash, a High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) architecture that exploits the large capacity of Quad-Level Cell (QLC)-based flash to realize CDA. However, QLC's long read latency demands massive read parallelism under irregular state reactivation and varying context lengths, while limited write endurance constrains placement. LaFlash introduces Session Grouping to balance active request counts and aggregate context lengths across groups, sustaining read parallelism and block utilization through request-exclusive allocation. Furthermore, Fast-Page Allocation exploits QLC's read-latency heterogeneity to mitigate residual inter-group imbalance and sustain bandwidth utilization. On end-to-end coding agent workloads, LaFlash achieves 7.04$\times$ higher throughput and 10.96$\times$ higher energy efficiency over SLC-HBF with batch expansion, and 2.36$\times$ higher throughput over QLC-HBF with CDA. HBM buffering further reduces unnecessary NAND writes, improving QLC write endurance. These results demonstrate the benefits of jointly optimizing state retention and physical data placement for capacity-driven acceleration.

papers.title: Construction and regularity of lump solutions of the modified KP-I equation
papers.abstract: We express the $τ$-functions of standard and higher-order lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I (mKP-I) equation as Gram determinants in integral form. Unlike the KP-I equation, the mKP-I $τ$-function is complex-valued, and its nonvanishing does not follow from the positive definiteness of a Hermitian Gram matrix. We derive explicit spectral conditions for the regularity of these solutions; for higher-order lumps, the sharp condition depends only on the spectral parameter and the largest entry of the index vector. We also prove that the lump solutions and all their spatial derivatives decay algebraically in every spatial direction, uniformly on compact time intervals.

papers.title: On Traffic Characterization in Time-Sensitive Networking and Deterministic Networking
papers.abstract: The traffic of an audio/video stream in IEEE Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) or an asynchronous traffic flow in IETF Deterministic Networking is specified by three parameters: an observation time interval, a maximum packet size, and a maximum number of packets in the interval. This traffic specification (TSpec) triggers three fundamental questions for TSN and DetNet: (1) if and how the traffic of a flow can be specified by these parameters after it traverses a system, (2) how to specify the traffic of a flow aggregate using the three parameters, and (3) how to use it in performance guarantee analysis. Among them, the literature has focused on (3), leaving the other two little investigated and largely open. This paper is intended to bridge the gap. Specifically, we introduce an equivalent traffic characterization for TSN TSpec, which is simple in representation and simplifies analytical development. Based on this result, we establish an output characterization property for (1) and show that the output of a TSN flow traversing a bounded-delay system can be characterized by the TSN TSpec with updated parameters. For (2) we study the superposition of TSN flows and derive TSN traffic characterizations for the aggregate of multiple TSN flows. For (3), based on a relationship between the TSN traffic characterization and the well-known token-bucket traffic characterization, backlog and delay bounds are derived. Together, these results form a calculus for TSN traffic characterization.

papers.title: Stochastic Diversity Windows: Diagnosing Noise Influence in Robotic Diffusion Sampling
papers.abstract: Diffusion models are increasingly adopted in robotics and control due to their capability to express multiple feasible solutions to a given task. However, the role of stochasticity in the diffusion model-sampler across denoising remains poorly understood. We introduce a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output. Across five model-sampler configurations spanning three robotics benchmarks, diverse architectures, domains, and conditioning mechanisms, we reveal highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles, where noise-induced deviations can amplify, partially contract, or undergo near-total attenuation downstream. From these profiles, we define stochastic diversity windows (SDWs): compact intervals that identify where sampler stochasticity has the strongest measured influence on the final output. Guided by these windows, we apply two heuristic interventions: targeted stochastic amplification, which increases sample diversity exploration of the solution space, and an SDW-hybrid sampler, which replaces DDPM steps with DDIM skips in low-impact regions, resulting in network evaluation reductions of up to 40-60% and wall-clock time by up to 85%, with no consistent changes detected in feasibility, cost, or diversity across held-out tasks.

papers.title: GaussianMamba: Geometric and Relational State Space Scanning of 3D Gaussian Primitives
papers.abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction requires representing complex spatial structures and modeling contextual relationships across a scene. 3D Gaussian primitives provide a sparse and adaptive representation of scene geometry and semantics, while Mamba offers efficient sequence modeling for capturing dependencies among primitives. However, Gaussian primitives are irregular and unordered, making sequence construction challenging, as conventional spatial ordering may overlook their anisotropic geometry and feature-semantic relationships. In this paper, we present GaussianMamba, a dual-branch Mamba framework that explicitly incorporates Gaussian-specific geometric and feature-semantic relationships into complementary scanning strategies. The first branch refines a locality-preserving traversal using anisotropic Gaussian support derived from primitive scale and orientation. The second branch reorders spatially organized groups according to feature-semantic affinity and adjusts local features using geometry-weighted semantic differences. The resulting sequences are processed by separate Mamba modules, and their features are fused through a support-aware mechanism that incorporates local feature discrepancies arising from the distinct scanning paths. Experiments on nuScenes-SurroundOcc and SSCBench-KITTI-360 demonstrate consistent improvements over GaussianFormer and GaussianFormer-2 in both IoU and mIoU.

papers.title: Semisimplicity of Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional complex algebra is semisimple if its Jacobson radical is zero. In this paper, we determine the complex parameters for which Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types are semisimple. We also determine semisimplicity at zero for the specified polynomial diagram forms and show that it can depend on the choice of polynomial form.

papers.title: AI as Anchor: How Interview Sequencing Relates to the Appropriation of Synthetic Stakeholder Voices in Design Education
papers.abstract: Designers increasingly use large language models to simulate stakeholder conversations. Yet it remains unclear how AI-Simulated Stakeholders (AIS) are taken up when used alongside human stakeholder engagement. We report a field study in a single-institution, single-semester design course in which 8 teams (N=21) constructed, evaluated, and peer-reviewed an initial AIS. Then, the teams interviewed both AIS and human stakeholders in two sequences: AIS-first or human-first. Drawing on interview transcripts, design artifacts, course-embedded reflections, and post-course qualitative sessions, we examine exploratory patterns associated with these sequencing conditions. We find that students did not describe AIS as a neutral addition to the process. Instead, the order in which AIS and human stakeholders were formally interviewed was associated with different ways of interpreting and using information from the two sources. When the AIS interview came first, it provided a broad but often general frame that students later reconsidered through human interviews. When the AIS interview followed human engagement, AIS was more often used to revisit and validate insights already grounded in lived experience. Students described AIS as an "anchor," but its reported role varied with its position in the formal interview sequence. In the final designs, a larger proportion of prominent human-stakeholder-derived concerns than AIS-derived concerns had corresponding design elements. We contribute: characterization of AIS as a reference point whose reported role varies with its position in the formal interview sequence; exploratory empirical evidence that the implemented interview-order conditions were associated with distinct patterns of interpreting and using stakeholder input; and implications for integrating AIS into design workflows in ways that preserve direct engagement with human stakeholders

papers.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.abstract: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

papers.title: Can Activation Steering Substitute for Prompt-Based Affective Priming in LLM Digital Twins?
papers.abstract: Affective priming -- asking participants to write about a recalled event, such as a time they felt grateful or lacked control, and then measuring the induced state and its spillover onto related judgments -- is a standard way to manipulate emotion in the social sciences, and it also shifts the responses of LLM-based digital twins. The writing task, however, requires generating a full text. We test whether activation steering can replace it. Using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 100 personas in two domains (gratitude, lack of control), we compare a real-prompt path replicating the original Twin-2K-500 Mega Study (J2) with an injection path that skips the writing and adds a mean-difference direction, extracted from human writing, to the residual stream at varying strengths. The real-prompt effects fall between the original human and digital-twin effects in 5 of 6 comparisons. Injection shifts the manipulation check in a dose-dependent way and matches the real-prompt effect at one strength in the gratitude domain (beta ~ 2.7), but overshoots beyond it, on the proximal measure as well, and asymmetrically across the two directions. A structure-matched No-Injection baseline separates two sources of difference: omitting the writing task raises the proximal measure in both domains, whereas the injected direction itself moves a distal measure in the lack-of-control domain. Substitution is therefore measure-dependent: validity established for one way of inducing a state does not carry over uniformly to another.

papers.title: Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers
papers.abstract: Looped refiners such as HRM and TRM apply one small network repeatedly to a draft answer, and deep supervision trains every pass toward one stored answer per puzzle. We prove that when a puzzle has many correct answers this target sets a loss floor that no model capacity removes, and that the loss-minimising pass blends the answers into an invalid grid. We propose the proximal target: train each pass toward the correct answer nearest to its own input, found by scanning a list of answers, by a search solver started at the draft, or within a band of quality set by a knob; correct answers become fixed points, and a pass only has to make fewer errors than its input has for the loop to converge, which its training loss bounds. With the same 1.7M-parameter network and 5 seeds, the proximal target solves 98.8% of Sudoku puzzles with 2-64 answers (standard target: 2.5%), 93.8% of sparse puzzles with more than 10,000 answers without any list of answers (0.0%), and 90.9% of 200-node 3-colourings after training on graphs of at most 50 nodes (36.9%), and different random starts end at different answers. Against GRAM, a stochastic-latent reasoner, a single run is correct far more often (98.8% vs. 57.7%) and twenty runs find more of the answers (53.6% vs. 37.4%), while GRAM is slightly ahead on its own 10-node colouring benchmark; in Scrabble the knob becomes a calibrated strength dial.

papers.title: RefCloth: Transferable Adversarial Tablecloths for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Closed-loop vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely continuously on multi-view cameras, yet existing visual attacks typically hijack sensor streams with 2D patches or alter target object meshes that require retraining when manipulation objects change. We introduce RefCloth, a framework that optimizes one persistent adversarial tablecloth on a frozen source policy and deploys it zero-shot across unseen tasks and target models without modifying task objects or cameras. Throughout manipulation, static third-person and moving wrist views observe this shared world-bound texture under evolving occlusions. To generalize across shifting surface views while bridging the gap between differentiable and native renderers, RefCloth combines bounded texture parameterization with shared surface UV transformations and a same-path clean reference that removes static rendering offsets at initialization. Across four LIBERO suites in native simulation, one frozen texture transfers from OpenVLA-OFT to $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$, reducing success relative to an unoptimized cloth by 62.50 and 43.75 percentage points on average and far exceeding amplitude- and variation-matched random controls. Dual-view audits and target closed-loop camera interventions show that moving wrist exposure drives over twice the standalone drop of the main view with strong synergy, while ablations confirm the roles of UV diversification and path calibration.

papers.title: Spin-Adapted Neural-Network Backflow Wavefunctions for Excited States of Strongly Correlated Open-Shell Systems
papers.abstract: Building on the success of neural-network quantum states (NQS) for molecular ground states, multi-state frameworks such as natural excited states (NES) [Pfau et al., Science 2024, 385, eadn0137] extend NQS to chemically important excited states. However, without control over total spin, such calculations can require the inclusion of many intervening states of other spins, particularly in strongly correlated systems with dense low-energy spectra. We therefore generalize our previously developed spin-adapted neural network backflow (SA-NNBF) ansatz [Li et al., arXiv:2604.06841 (2026)] to improve its variational flexibility for excited-state calculations within a prescribed spin sector. We establish the universality of this extended ansatz within the chosen orbital space and spin sector, and use numerical benchmarks to assess how parameter allocation affects the ansatz's accuracy. With the spin-adapted ansatz, we are able to directly optimize the first excited state (a singlet) of $O_2$ without using any multi-state frameworks. Combining the extended ansatz with NES, we obtain low-lying triplet states of $O_2$ and singlet states of the $[\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{S}_2(\mathrm{SCH}_3)_4]^{2-}$ cluster without including intervening states of other spins. Both the single-state and NES calculations achieve chemical accuracy relative to the exact energies. Our work provides a practical NQS framework for targeting excited states of prescribed spin in strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: Catalytic imaginarity transformations
papers.abstract: State conversion is a central problem in quantum resource theories. In this work, we investigate catalytic state transformations within the resource theory of imaginarity. Catalytic imaginarity transformations enable otherwise impossible state transformations using only real operations, assisted by an auxiliary system with imaginarity that is not consumed. For deterministic catalytic conversion, we show that a maximally imaginary pure state is the unique catalyst. This result contrasts with the resource theories of entanglement and coherence, where maximally entangled and maximally coherent catalysts cannot enable such deterministic conversions under their respective free operations. For stochastic-approximate catalytic conversion, if we do not require catalyst recovery upon failure, any pure state with imaginarity can serve as a catalyst, and we derive the optimal success probability. If the catalyst is required to be recovered exactly regardless of whether the catalytic state transformation succeeds or fails, the optimal success probability coincides with that without a catalyst, and thus no advantage arises from catalysis. If exact catalyst recovery upon failure is relaxed, we find a tradeoff relation between the success probability of a single conversion and the catalyst's residual imaginarity after transformation. When the initial state is re-prepared and the catalyst's residual imaginarity can be reused after failure, the success probability can be further improved over $N$ ($N \geq 2$) rounds of catalytic conversion, and we obtain the corresponding maximum overall success probability.

papers.title: Evolve in Panorama, Render in View: Panoramic World State Evolution for Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models should maintain a world that keeps evolving as the viewpoint changes. Yet when the camera turns away and returns, current models often freeze the unobserved scene, lose objects, or change their appearance, because content outside the view has no representation that keeps changing. We present PanoEvo, which uses a Panoramic Evolver to evolve the world state in the latent space of a panoramic video diffusion model, where every viewing direction is present at every time step, so the scene evolves whether or not it is observed. Existing panoramic video models are not trained to evolve a scene from a single image or the objects within it, so we build PanoEvo-Data, an event-centric dataset from real 360° videos, and train the Panoramic Evolver coarse-to-fine as an image-to-panoramic-video model. Since each view covers only a small part of the low-resolution panorama, directly projected views are blurry and often show low-quality details or structural errors. A Perspective Renderer, built on a perspective video diffusion model, reads this state via latent-space projection and direction-restricted cross-attention to render sharp, high-quality views. PanoEvo achieves the best overall score among 23 publicly evaluated models on WRBench and the highest total score on STEVO-Bench. Code, models, and data will be released.

papers.title: Provable Mixing Properties of Parallel Mixnets Revisited
papers.abstract: A mix-network (mixnet) is a routing network that breaks source-to-destination message trackability by indistinguishably mixing the routes of concurrently transmitted messages, thus providing anonymity to senders, receivers and sender-receiver pairs. Given their potential use in high-stakes scenarios like protecting whistleblowers, one would like to prove formally that sender anonymity holds in a mixnet, even against strong adversaries that can compromise subsets of mixnet servers. However, existing work on anonymity in mixnets is either limited to linear mixnets (which do not scale horizontally), relies on special provisions such as additional noise or chaff messages, or is empirical -- typically based on entropy, which does not provide strong guarantees if the adversary has auxiliary information. In this paper, we present a new analysis of parallel mixnets which scale horizontally, showing that these networks can provide strong indistinguishability for messages even without additional noise messages. Our analysis works by bounding the statistical variance of the adversary's posterior likelihood of where a message of interest is at a given point in time. Using concentration bounds on this distribution, we show that parallel mixnets satisfy $(\varepsilon, δ)$-differential indistinguishability for messages routed through the mixnet (similar to $(\varepsilon, δ)$-differential privacy) with very small failure probabilities $δ$ and small privacy parameters $\varepsilon$ under reasonable operating conditions. Our model also enables an examination of the quantitative trade-off between anonymity, latency and per-router bandwidth in parallel mixnets.

papers.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
papers.abstract: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.

papers.title: Covariate-Indexed Inclusion Probabilities on Unbalanced Panels
papers.abstract: We estimate the probability that an item with given covariates belongs to a set when the cross-section changes over time and items and periods are dependent. We propose two convex models whose fitted probabilities are nonnegative by construction and remain valid whatever the dependence between items, for which we establish consistency, finite-sample bounds and limit distributions for serially dependent panels. One suits events of moderate or high probability, the other rare events, and half the disagreement between their fits estimates a lower bound on the misspecification error of the worse fit, without knowledge of the true probabilities. On monthly US stock failures, the rare-event model predicts better than the ordinary logit and the classical failure logit. With the eight classical predictors, most of the gain comes from basis functions of the rank angle of each predictor and summary.

papers.title: Optical rectification and Pockels effect in the organic nonlinear crystal MBI for quasi-discrete THz time-domain spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Organic nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals offer efficient nonlinear frequency conversion for broadband THz spectroscopy. Unfortunately, only a subset of NLO crystals is compatible with the telecom (~1.5 $μ$m) pump wavelength region, where convenient MHz-rate femtosecond fiber lasers are available. Here, we present ultra-broadband (1-30 THz) THz generation and detection using a benzoindolium iodide (MBI, C$_{24}$H$_{24}$NOI) crystal illuminated by a 1.5 $μ$m MHz-rate fiber laser. At 200 mW of average pump power, the crystal delivers ~1 $μ$W of THz radiation as quasi-discrete peaks covering the whole emission region with a prominent peak at 11.8 THz. High-dynamic range (>40 dB) time-domain spectroscopy is demonstrated within minutes of integration.

papers.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen computation by reusing shared layers, approaching larger models' capabilities with fewer parameters and easing the storage and deployment burden of stacking independent layers. However, repeatedly processing long visual sequences still incurs substantial compute and GPU memory costs. Visual token compression reduces these costs by shortening sequences. Existing methods mainly select original tokens directly or combine selection with aggregation. In looped models, the former may overlook changing token importance across calls and discard information needed later; the latter lack joint consideration of output changes across calls, limiting information preservation. We propose LoopZip, a training-free visual token compression algorithm addressing both issues. Visual aggregation builds a compact candidate pool before the looped backbone, and cross-invocation selection averages instruction attention from the first two existing calls of the same shared attention layer to retain tokens needed by both states. Weight-tied value correction then jointly fits shared visual-value adjustments to both pre-selection layer outputs, reducing output deviations across states. To validate LoopZip's effectiveness, we conduct extensive experiments covering two open-source looped VLMs, eleven benchmarks, and three pruning ratios. On LoopVL-1B, LoopZip retains 97.16% of the original model's performance at 50% pruning ratio and exceeds the strongest baseline by 5.36% at 87.5% pruning ratio. Across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang, LoopVL-1B with LoopZip reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 58.36%-58.98% and achieves 2.01-2.47x end-to-end speedups over the original model.

papers.title: SlopeGuard: Towards Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection via Radial Spectral Slope Guidance
papers.abstract: AI-generated image detectors often overfit to generator-specific artifacts, hindering generalization to unseen synthesis pipelines. Existing frequency-based methods usually learn high-dimensional spectral patterns that may preserve generator-dependent variations. We explore Radial Spectral Slope, a compact descriptor of global spectral decay that captures transferable spectral trends while suppressing fine-grained variations. Our analysis shows that real and generated images exhibit systematic but generator-dependent slope differences, indicating that slope provides useful forensic evidence but is insufficient as a standalone decision criterion. This motivates combining spectral slope with semantic representations for more robust detection. Based on this insight, we propose SlopeGuard, which couples slope-aware data processing with slope guided feature learning to construct informative patch-based views, integrate Radial Spectral Slope with semantic features, and adapt prior preservation according to spectral atypicality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SlopeGuard achieves state-of-the-art mean accuracies of 97.5% on AIGCDetectBench, 97.8% on GenImage, and 85.1% on AIGIBench, while maintaining competitive performance under blur, cropping, JPEG compression, and additive noise.

papers.title: Stress Testing a Multimodal Large Language Model Grading Assistant on Kinematics Graph Reading
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can recognize graph features yet award credit without sufficient graphical support. This exploratory study examines selected grading outputs for synthetic responses to four kinematics exercises, generated through visual distortion and progressive transformation toward reference graphs. Different model and prompt configurations were used. Some judgments correctly distinguished instantaneous zero velocity from rest over a finite interval and recognized positive curvature. Yet a severely distorted velocity--time graph received full credit despite disconnected and branching traces and an unclear zero-velocity reference. Other submissions graded under the same configuration lost substantial credit. Numerical cutoffs intended to distinguish meaningful features from drawing irregularities were supplied without a coordinate convention for unnumbered graphs, leaving the basis of exact partial-credit awards unresolved. Stress testing can expose unsupported awards before classroom use. For the configurations examined, we do not recommend accepting scores as final grades without instructor review, including review of full-credit responses.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves Population Study for Testing Kerr Hypothesis: Are Non-Kerr Deformations Universal or Source-Dependent?
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of binary black hole mergers can test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field and dynamical regime. In our previous works, we constrained the deformation parameters $α_{13}$ and $ε_3$ of the Johannsen metric using individual inspiral-dominated events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 and found no evidence of deviations from the Kerr solution. Here we combine 17 of these events to test whether black holes are Kerr, share a common non-zero deformation, or have deformations that vary from source to source. We first estimate the Savage--Dickey Bayes factor of each event, and we test how it depends on the prior range and on the removal of single events. We then combine the event likelihoods assuming a universal deformation, yielding a tighter joint constraint. Next, we perform a simple hierarchical analysis by assuming that the event-level deformation parameters are drawn from a population with mean $μ$ and intrinsic scatter $σ$. A universal deformation is constrained to $α_{13}=-0.01^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $ε_3=0.06^{+0.59}_{-0.54}$. The means from the population are consistent with zero for both parameters, and the scatter is not resolved by the current data. Our results are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis, but they cannot yet distinguish a shared deformation from a source-dependent one.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: Prompt J/psi Cross-Section Measurements in pp and Peripheral PbPb Collisions at sqrt(S)= 7 TeV and sqrt(sNN) = 2.76 TeV
papers.abstract: We investigate the use of an artificial-intelligence (AI) coding agent, supervised by human physicists, for collider physics analyses using CMS Open Data. OpenAI Codex performs dimuon event selection, two-dimensional invariant-mass and decay-length fits, Monte Carlo detector simulations, and systematic uncertainty evaluation after acquiring physics and experimental knowledge from published studies and external references, with human review at each stage. The workflow is tested on two CMS datasets, with custom full-detector simulations used to determine acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies. In proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV, prompt J/psi differential cross sections are measured versus transverse momentum and rapidity. The ratios of remeasured to published CMS cross sections have a mean of 1.000 and an RMS spread of 0.215 across 39 bins. In peripheral (50-100% centrality) PbPb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV, the corresponding prompt J/psi fiducial cross-section ratios have a mean of 1.158 and an RMS spread of 0.225 across six intervals. We identify agent failure modes and demonstrate the importance of structured human review in ensuring reliable results.

papers.title: Practice in Text, Act in Pixels: Correcting Where Perception Fails
papers.abstract: GUI agents can learn cheaply from a text view of an interface and act on screenshots through a vision-language screen reader. Yet on a simulated mobile platform with a low-cost reader, policies that complete most tasks in text fail on many of the same tasks on screenshots. We ask where a small budget of real screenshots is best spent to close this gap. We find that the reader's misreads are systematic and recur on the same interface elements. Noise matched to the reader's error rates, a natural sim-to-real remedy, misses this structure, and in a pre-specified comparison it did not beat training the policy directly on screenshots. We therefore correct the misreads at their source with reader alignment, which fine-tunes the reader on screenshots paired with their text views. The reader learns to output each screen's text view, as in text practice, and the policy stays unchanged. Spent on the reader, the screenshot budget gives 80.9% full-task success on new task instances, against 55.6% when spent on training the policy. Given the same labeled screenshots, adapting the reader also beats adapting the policy, and a single aligned reader improves every text-trained policy we tried without retraining any of them.

papers.title: HADVQ: Hessian Aware Directional Vector Quantization
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-bit quantization of large language models is a challenging task because aggressive compression severely distorts model parameters and disproportionately harms a small number of highly sensitive channels. We present a vector quantization method tailored for this regime. Our approach begins with random preconditioning, which regularizes the weight space and makes it more amenable to quantization. We then represent weights in polar coordinates and decouple the quantization of directions and magnitudes. To quantize directions, we leverage the structure induced by random preconditioning and design a structured codebook based on the $E_8$ lattice, yielding a compact yet expressive representation. To further reduce degradation, we detect extremely important channels using a proxy Hessian and preserve them with an additional cost of only 0.16 bits. Together, these components provide an effective quantization pipeline for LLMs in the extremely low-bit regime. Empirical results demonstrate improved accuracy, highlighting the benefit of combining geometric structure, lattice-based codebooks, and selective channel preservation.

papers.title: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
papers.abstract: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$. We prove that $a_k(n)\ge0$ for all $k,n\ge0$, thereby resolving a conjecture on signed odd-multiplicity partitions. Our proof combines a positive theta--MacMahon factorization for the generating functions restricted to odd part sizes with a dyadic product decomposition that extends positivity to arbitrary part sizes. Moreover, we establish strict positivity $a_k(n)>0$ for every $k\ge2$ and $n\ge\binom{k+1}{2}$.

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $Ω_{gw}(f)/Ω_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.

papers.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Reference-to-video diffusion transformers pack the variational autoencoder (VAE) latents of all references and the generated tokens into one full-attention sequence, in which reference tokens make up about half. Because attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, these tokens take up an even larger share of the attention computation, yet most of them are static, smooth or irrelevant to the output.
